proof:
# One arc stress for all nonatomic curvature source patterns

This theorem combines candidate f27caa3ee43c68e2,
candidate ed7be0e1efdfe13b, and the independently audited
curvature-potential-locality-on-singular-support.md. It removes the need for
mutual absolute continuity among different fibers' diffuse curvature.
The stable support-contact and cap-membership interval hypothesis remains.

## 1. Setting and the measurable source patterns

Fix an attained local mixed-depth minimum with finite positive planar fibers,
total area M, depth beta>0, and a finite exact critical/slack cap cover. On an
open normal interval I, every chosen cap has a fixed strict membership on
each affected fiber boundary arc. A fixed finite list of linear Jensen
support equalities holds identically on I, with coefficient kernel L. Other
support inequalities have positive gaps on every compact interval used.

Let R_z=h_z+h_z'' be each fiber's finite nonnegative curvature measure, and
write R_z^c for its nonatomic part. Define

    R=sum_z R_z^c,       r_z=dR_z^c/dR.

Thus r_z>=0 and sum_z r_z=1, R-almost everywhere. For each nonempty subset
J of the finite fiber indices, let

    E_J={theta:r_z(theta)>0 exactly for z in J},
    L_J=L intersect {v:v_z=0 for z outside J}.

The E_J form a finite measurable partition modulo an R-null set. For each
positive integer k put

    nu_Jk=(1/k) 1_(E_J intersect {min_(z in J) r_z>=1/k}) R.  (1)

Zero measures are ignored. Every nonzero nu_Jk is nonatomic and is dominated
by every R_z for z in J. The countable union of their supporting measurable
sets covers E_J up to R-null sets. Restricting further to compact subintervals
of I, when needed for compact support, does not change this exhaustion.

## 2. All second-order generators coexist in one realizable cone

For any v in L_J and nonzero measure nu_Jk, the Green-potential construction
gives a compactly supported signed variation delta h_z=v_z phi, where

    phi''+phi=psi nu_Jk,
    integral phi dR_z=0 for EVERY fiber z,
    integral(phi^2-phi'^2)<0.

The two sine/cosine moment constraints make the potential and its derivative
vanish outside its compact interval. Bounded psi and domination in (1)
preserve all curvature measures for both signs of a sufficiently small
parameter. Because v lies in L, compatibility equalities remain exact.
The inactive gaps and cap memberships persist by uniform smallness.

Different generators may use different, even overlapping, source measures.
Every FINITE list can nevertheless be put on pairwise disjoint intervals.
Inductively choose distinct points in their supports: a nonzero nonatomic
measure is not supported on any finite set. Choose disjoint small intervals
around those points; each has positive mass for its own source measure.
Perform the finitely many orthogonality equations separately in each such
interval. Rescale each potential's negative interval energy as desired.

Thus every finite conic combination of ALL the vectors

    B(v)=(-sum_z v_z^2, -sum_z I_jz v_z^2 for each cap j),
    v in L_J,        R(E_J)>0,                               (2)

is the second mass vector of one actual feasible perturbation with every
first body and cap mass zero. It is not necessary that two source patterns
contain disjoint supports or that a uniform parameter work for infinitely
many perturbations.

## 3. Countably many sources still have a finite acceleration model

Allow first-order acceleration tests generated by ALL compact Green
potentials from all the nu_Jk, imposing only their two endpoint moments;
the additional zero-mass equations are not needed for acceleration tests.
Take their algebraic linear span. Each member uses only finitely many
potentials and remains a signed feasible support variation by domination.

Its effect on the objective and on every fixed cap factors through

    U_z(delta h)=integral delta h_z dR_z,

a vector in the fixed finite-dimensional space R^P. The image of the entire
countable source family therefore has a finite basis. Choose finitely many
actual potential tests realizing that basis. These retain all first mass
effects of every source test, with no limiting interchange.

Adjoin signed common continuous homotheties and the finite cap-acceleration
coordinates satisfying the exact linear whole-fiber-cover constraints. This
is the same finite acceleration cone as in the direct-budget theorem. The
compact consistent cap-gradient sets are unchanged: their dependence on
the body acceleration is only through U and the homothety coefficient.

Apply that theorem's robust epigraph separation to the cone generated by
ALL vectors (2). Its open-orthant separation does not require this cone to
be closed. The two exact joint homotheties again normalize the separator.
We obtain ONE set of cap weights lambda_j>=0, independent of J and k, with

    sum_j lambda_j=1/beta,
    W_z=1-sum_j lambda_j I_jz,
    sum_z W_z v_z^2>=0 for every v in L_J whenever R(E_J)>0.  (3)

The same stress annihilates every first-order potential test from every
source pattern, because their finite feature image was retained.

## 4. Locality gives the curvature nullspace on every pattern

Fix J and v in L_J. Put the signed measure

    mu_v=sum_z W_z v_z R_z.

For each nu_Jk and each admissible compact Green potential phi, first-order
annihilation gives integral phi dmu_v=0. The potential-locality lemma shows

    (mu_v)^c restricted to supp(nu_Jk)=0.                    (4)

This is the NONATOMIC restriction. Atoms of the signed curvature measure
are not removed by an argument using a nonatomic source. The lemma does not
require the source support to contain an interval: its potential agrees
with a harmonic function on that support, and BV locality removes the
diffuse second derivative there.

Taking Radon--Nikodym derivatives in (4) yields

    sum_z W_z v_z r_z=0    nu_Jk-almost everywhere.

Use a finite basis of L_J and then the countable exhaustion in k. We conclude

    diag(W) r(theta) is orthogonal to L_J
                      for R-almost every theta in E_J.      (5)

The active support equalities also hold distributionally after applying
D^2+1. Their nonatomic parts give the same linear relations among the r_z.
On E_J the other coordinates vanish, so

    r(theta) belongs to L_J.                                (6)

Combining (3),(5),(6), the actual curvature-density vector lies almost
everywhere on E_J in the nullspace of ONE positive-semidefinite diagonal
form restricted to L_J. The weights W are common to all source patterns.
In particular any positive-measure occurring pattern has a nonzero vector
in L_J which is strictly positive on every coordinate of J.

The result handles mutually singular diffuse curvature measures by splitting
their actual source patterns rather than assuming a common positive density.
It leaves curvature atoms, cap-crossing normal intervals, and arbitrary
changes of active support relations as separate global obligations.
